subject: Recap + next steps: competitive contrast matrix, POC scope & procurement asks
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Cole <hannah@medtech.ai>, Jared Liu <jared.liu@procurements.medtech.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: competitive contrast matrix, POC scope & procurement asks

Hi Hannah / Jared — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap below so we keep alignment while you brief the procurement and engineering teams. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level pain (what you told us)
- Inference cost is unpredictable across peak loads; current cloud spend for embedding & generation is a material line item.
- Latency spikes during batch processing are impacting near-real-time clinical workflows (need p95 < 250ms target on typical patient cohort).
- Security/regulatory: must be able to run inside your VPC/on-prem for PHI, and supply SOC2 + audit logs for model activity.
- Model flexibility: want ability to unify hosted and private runtimes so R&D can iterate on model variants without app changes.

Goals / success metrics you shared
- Reduce per-inference token cost by ~3x (or show path to it via batching/quantization).
- p95 latency <= 250ms for 4k-ish sequences on a reserved pool (initial target).
- Proof of concept that demonstrates VPC private deployment + signed audit logs.

Where Redwood helps (summary)
- Single API with drop-in routing between hosted/dedicated/private so SDK calls don’t change.
- Autoscaling dedicated pools, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles that typically show 2–4x unit cost improvement depending on traffic shape.
- Private deployment options + KMS/HSM integrations; we’ll provide SOC2 artifacts and an architecture diagram for your security review.

Competitive context we discussed
- You mentioned evaluating two vendors internally: Vendor A (focus on managed endpoints) and Vendor B (on-prem only). We suggested a short contrast matrix during the POC to show where latency/cost/trust differ for your workload.

Suggested next steps (proposed timeline)
1) Technical deep-dive (1 hour) — engineering-to-engineering; goal: confirm sequence lengths, batching profile, and sampling traffic. (Target week of Mar 22)
2) POC scope doc (we’ll propose scope within 2 business days): tests, datasets, success thresholds (latency/cost/throughput).
3) Procurement checklist + SOC2 artifacts sent to Jared (this email attaches our TD guide).
4) Quick commercial signal: rough ballpark pricing for a 3-month reserved pool to help procurement.

Attachments: redwood-quick-td-guide.pdf (short TD + SOC2 checklist)

Open questions from our side
- Can you share a small representative tokenized trace or request profile (anonymized)? It helps us size the pool and set quant targets.
- Who on your side will own the POC success criteria (name + email)?

If that all looks right I’ll: 1) schedule the engineering deep-dive with Karthik, 2) draft the POC scope doc, and 3) send SOC2 + procurement checklist to Jared.

Thanks again — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through the scope.

—
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Mateo — helpful summary. Two clarifications before you draft the POC scope: 

1) Decision criteria (weighting): Security 35%, Latency/Availability 30%, Cost 25%, Integration effort 10%. Procurement will want clear pass/fail gates mapped to these weights.
2) Latency baseline: our production traces show p95 ~ 450ms today for the workflow you saw; p50 ~ 120ms. The 4k sequence estimate was correct for our worst-case.

Attached: medtech-rfp-v2.pdf (procurement updated the RFP; it includes our standard contract terms and insurance requirements).

We’ve looped procurement (Jared) who will handle legal/commercial. For the technical deep-dive, please include your SRE or solutions engineer who can talk about KV caching and dedicated pool sizing.

Quick ask: can you provide an example contrast-matrix template so we can see the fields procurement expects?

Regards,

Proposed internal split:
- Karthik: lead the tech deep-dive and own the test harness + test-matrix.csv (we’ll need a harness that reproduces p95 baseline and a small synthetic cohort for caching experiments).
- Marissa: lead commercial + procurement signal; prep an initial 3-month reserved estimate and identify any concessions (SLA credits / trial capacity).
- Mateo (me): draft POC scope and coordinate SOC2 + artifacts to Jared.

Immediate asks: Karthik, can you confirm availability for a deep-dive Mar 23–24 (preferably morning PST)? Can you also draft the initial test matrix and list of measurements we’ll capture (latency distribution p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost/token, cold-start time, KV hit ratio)?

Marissa, would you prepare a rough rate card for a small reserved capacity (3 months) and note any lead-time for private deployment? Hannah flagged procurement-weighting priorities — security heavy so we should be explicit about SOC2 and KMS/HSM options.

I’m attaching the TD guide I sent them for reference.

Thanks — I’m on it. Availability: Mar 23 morning PST looks good for a 60-minute deep-dive (I can do 9–11am PT).

Initial test plan (short):
- Ingest a 10k-row anonymized sample of requests (tokens per request, typical concurrency pattern).
- Run three baseline runs: hosted default, dedicated unoptimized, dedicated + prefix/KV caching + quantized model. Each run captures p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and end-to-end cost estimate.
- Measure cold-start (idle -> first token) and KV hit ratio with synthetic repeats.
- Produce a simple contrast matrix (CSV) with columns: vendor, deployment-mode, p95(ms), cost/token, tokens/sec, notes.

Open technical questions for the deep-dive (we should answer these in the session):
1) Are there any hard constraints on outbound connections from your VPC (we may need to pull container images or contact registry endpoints)?
2) Will PHI data be allowed in the test traces or do we need an anonymized dataset (we should get an anonymized sample if possible).
3) Expected concurrent clients and peak qps during worst-case windows.

I attached a starter test-matrix.csv and will flesh it out today. I’ll also prepare a minimal harness repo that can replay traces and collect token-level metrics.

Karthik
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
